chunks.text:

| 2 4. Groundwater Levels: About 43.1% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 37.6% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. About 19.2% of the total monitoring wells show water level deeper than 10 m below ground level. The groundwater level fluctuation analysis of Pre-monsoon 2025 with decadal mean of Pre-monsoon (2015-2024) indicates that 67.7% of analysed wells are showing rise and 33.0% are showing fall in water level. Remaining 0.3% stations analysed do not show any change in water level. As per the Ground Water Drought Indices (GWDI), in pre-monsoon 2025, 90% of the analysed wells are in the normal category, while 10% of the analysed wells are in the drought category. 5. Seeds and Fertilizers: For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Maize, Soyabean and Groundnut (White grub) in Maharashtra. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7. rows: 3. Water Reservoir Status: As on 17th July 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important

percent of last year's storage and 170 percent of the average storage of the last ten years
during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the
corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the
Normal storage during the corresponding period.

chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
- During the week (10 July - 16 July2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 11%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th June to 16th July 2025) is higher than LPA by 9%. Rainfall Forecast: - Overall, near normal to above normal rainfall activity is likely over central & south Peninsular India; near normal over most parts of east & northeast India; below normal rainfall activity is likely over most parts of northwest India during the week. - The Monsoon trough is active with its western end runs to the south of its normal position and eastern end north of its normal position at mean sea level. It is likely to shift northward during next 2 days.

chunks.heading: 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX
chunks.text:
Temerature Week 1 (18 July - 24 July 2025): - Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-3°C over Uttar Pradesh, most parts of east & adjoining central India, northeast India and along the west coast. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country. Week 2 (25 July - 31 July 2025): - Maximum temperatures are likely to be above normal by 2-3°C over north India including Western Himalayan Region and northeast India. These are likely to be below normal or near normal over rest parts of the country.
| 5


Current live storage in 161 reservoirs was 104.36 BCM (57%) of total live capacity of 182.46 BCM. chunks.heading: 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION
chunks.text:
Soil Moisture Observation - Soil moisture as on 18 July 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Southern West Bengal, Haryana and Western & Bundelkhand region of U.P. - It was lower than average of past 9 years in Northern and Central parts of Bihar, Eastern parts of U.P., Northern parts of West Bengal, Telangana, Assam and in parts of A.P., Karnataka and Maharashtra. | 7


Kharif Crops - Area coverage - Rice: About 176.68 lakh ha area coverage under Kharif Rice as compared to 157.21 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Soybean: About 111.67 lakh ha area coverage under Soyabean has been reported as compared to 118.96 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Sugarcane: About 55.16 lakh ha area coverage under Sugarcane has been reported as compared to 54.88 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Cotton: About 98.55 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 102.05 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year; Government of India Crops Division Progress of area coverage under Kharif crops as on 18.07.2025 Area: In lakh hectare S.
